presentingComplaint: Fever and rigors 9 days after chemotherapy for AML
history: Known acute myeloid leukaemia on induction chemotherapy (cytarabine + daunorubicin), day 9 post-cycle. Presents with a single spike of fever to 38.6 C with rigors this evening, mild sore mouth and fatigue. No localising cough, dysuria, diarrhoea or skin symptoms. Has a tunnelled central venous catheter in situ. No recent antibiotics; last hospitalisation was for this chemotherapy cycle. No known drug allergies.
examination: Ill but alert. Oral mucositis with shallow buccal ulcers. Central line exit site clean, non-tender, no erythema or discharge. Chest clear, abdomen soft and non-tender, no perianal cellulitis or fluctuance. No focus of infection identified on careful examination including skin, perineum and IV sites.
imaging: Chest radiograph clear; no consolidation. CT reserved for persistent fever or localising signs.
microbiology: Two sets of blood cultures drawn (peripheral + central line) before antibiotics; urine culture sent; results pending.
citations: Harrison 22e - Infections in Patients with Cancer
IDSA Clinical Practice Guideline for Antimicrobial Agents in Neutropenic Patients with Cancer 2010
stewardship: Empiric anti-pseudomonal beta-lactam monotherapy within 1 hour: IV piperacillin-tazobactam (or cefepime / meropenem). Add vancomycin only for suspected line infection, skin/soft-tissue focus, MRSA colonisation or haemodynamic instability; this patient does not yet meet those criteria. High-risk (MASCC-defined, prolonged profound neutropenia expected) so admit for IV therapy.
contraindications: Beta-lactam anaphylaxis - substitute aztreonam plus vancomycin; avoid aminoglycoside monotherapy; dose-adjust for renal impairment
edgeCases: A single temperature >=38.3 C (or >=38.0 C sustained 1h) with ANC <500 is sufficient to act; do NOT wait for a second spike or a localising focus
Neutropenic patients may mount minimal inflammatory signs (no infiltrate, no pus), so absence of a focus does not exclude serious infection
expectedMaiK: Fever with ANC <500/uL is an oncological emergency: give empiric anti-pseudomonal beta-lactam within 60 minutes after two sets of blood cultures, and reserve vancomycin for specific indications rather than routine addition.
expectedNextQuestions: Any central-line tenderness, erythema or discharge, or MRSA colonisation history?
Expected depth and duration of neutropenia / MASCC risk score?
expectedInvestigations: Paired peripheral and central-line blood cultures
Urinalysis and urine culture, chest radiograph, repeat FBC and CRP
regressionAssertions: empiric antibiotic must be an anti-pseudomonal beta-lactam (piperacillin-tazobactam/cefepime/meropenem)
vancomycin not added by default without a specific indication
